subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Bone sarcomas: osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma and chondrosarcoma

steps.tx: Primary bone malignancy displays distinctive anatomical predispositions and biological behaviors. **Osteosarcoma** typically arises in the metaphysis of adolescent long bones, defined histologically by malignant mesenchymal spindle cells producing immature osteoid matrix. Classical radiological hallmarks include periosteal elevation forming **Codman triangle**, aggressive cortical breakthrough, and extensive cloud-like osteoblastic mineralisation with sunburst periosteal reaction extending into adjacent soft tissues.

left.title: Osteosarcoma Features
points: Bimodal incidence: 10-20 yrs and >60 yrs (Paget)
Metaphyseal predilection (distal femur, proximal tibia)
Malignant osteoid production is diagnostic sine qua non
Codman triangle and sunburst periosteal reaction

right.title: Ewing Sarcoma Features
points: Peak incidence in children and young teens (5-15 yrs)
Diaphyseal or metadiaphyseal flat and long bones
Small round blue cell histology without matrix
Onion-skin lamellated multilayered periosteal reaction

steps.tx: The knee radiograph shows a destructive distal **femoral lesion** with fluffy cloud like **osteoid mineralisation**. Fine rays burst outward through the cortex as a **sunburst reaction**, lifting the periosteum into a **Codman triangle**. This aggressive metaphyseal pattern in a young patient is classic for osteosarcoma.
steps.say: Look at the lower end of the thigh bone near the knee. A cloudy white mass fills the metaphysis, with spiky bone rays streaming into the soft tissue and the lifted edge of periosteum forming a small triangle. That triad of cloud like mineral, sunburst reaction and Codman triangle defines osteosarcoma, usually in teenagers. Any such lesion needs urgent referral to a specialist bone tumour center without prior poorly planned biopsy.

vis.alt: A knee radiograph shows a distal femoral lesion with sunburst reaction and Codman triangle.
vis.caption: Cloud like mineral with sunburst change marks osteosarcoma. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Osteosarcoma classically shows a **Codman triangle**, where the lifted periosteum is bridged by new bone at its edges, and a sunburst periosteal reaction. Ewing sarcoma instead shows an **onion-skin** periosteal reaction from layered new bone. Both tumours are aggressive and destructive, so imaging must be read alongside histology before treatment begins.

steps.tx: Neoadjuvant multi-agent systemic chemotherapy followed by definitive surgical resection forms the foundation of modern osteosarcoma management. Standard curative therapy for localized osteosarcoma is neoadjuvant and adjuvant **MAP chemotherapy** high-dose methotrexate with **leucovorin** rescue, doxorubicin, and cisplatin combined with limb-sparing surgical resection. Pathological tumour necrosis of 90% or greater in the resected specimen defines a **good histological response**.

nodes.label: Limb-Sparing En Bloc Resection with Clear Margins

steps.tx: Specific pathognomonic chromosomal translocations drive gene dysregulation in primitive neuroectodermal bone tumours. **Ewing sarcoma** is characterized by the reciprocal translocation **t(11;22)**(q24;q12) in approximately 85% to 90% of cases, creating the aberrantly functioning EWSR1-FLI1 chimeric transcription factor. On histological examination, tumour sheets comprise uniform small round blue cells with diastase-sensitive cytoplasmic glycogen demonstrating intense membranous CD99 MIC2 positivity.

rows: Diagnostic confirmation via FISH or RT-PCR
Occurs in approximately 10% of atypical cases

steps.tx: Intensifying chemotherapy delivery intervals improves curative outcomes in localized Ewing family tumours. The five-drug alternating **VDC/IE regimen** combines **vincristine**, **doxorubicin**, and **cyclophosphamide** alternating with **ifosfamide** and **etoposide**. In the randomized prospective AEWS0031 trial, administering chemotherapy every 2 weeks using **interval compression** with filgrastim support significantly improved event-free and overall survival compared to standard 3-week cycles without increasing cumulative toxicities.
steps.say: Intensifying chemotherapy delivery intervals improves curative outcomes in localized Ewing family tumours. The five-drug alternating VDC/IE regimen combines vincristine, doxorubicin, and cyclophosphamide alternating with ifosfamide and etoposide. In clinical trials, administering chemotherapy every 2 weeks using interval compression with filgrastim support significantly improved event-free and overall survival.

nodes.label: Cycle B: Ifosfamide + Etoposide Alternate Infusion

steps.tx: Cartilage-forming malignancies display intrinsic insensitivity to standard medical oncology modalities. **Chondrosarcoma** is an intrinsically chemoresistant and radioresistant malignancy characterized by abundant avascular extracellular matrix, slow replication kinetics, and expression of multidrug-resistance transport pumps. Wide **surgical excision** with negative margins remains the sole curative modality for localized conventional and dedifferentiated chondrosarcomas, as cytotoxic chemotherapy and photon radiotherapy fail to alter survival.

left.title: Conventional Chondrosarcoma
points: Dense, avascular hyaline chondroid extracellular matrix
Intrinsically chemoresistant and radioresistant
Overexpresses multidrug resistance transport proteins
Cure achieved exclusively through complete R0 resection

right.title: Dedifferentiated / Mesenchymal
points: High-grade bimorphic histology with spindle cell component
Mesenchymal variant displays HEY1-NCOA2 gene fusion
Mesenchymal component shows modest chemo responsiveness
Early haematogenous dissemination to pulmonary parenchyma

steps.tx: Metabolic oncogenic driver alterations represent novel therapeutic targets in central cartilaginous neoplasms. Somatic mutations in **IDH1 and IDH2** occur in up to 50% of central chondrosarcomas, producing the oncometabolite **2-hydroxyglutarate** 2-HG from alpha-ketoglutarate. Accumulation of 2-HG inhibits alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent histone demethylases and TET methylcytosine dioxygenases, leading to genome-wide DNA hypermethylation and impaired cellular differentiation, an actionable target for selective IDH inhibitors.

nodes.label: Inhibition of TET Enzymes & Histone Demethylases

steps.tx: Isolated pulmonary recurrence represents a unique potentially curable oligometastatic state in sarcomas. **Pulmonary metastasectomy** achieved via complete surgical resection of isolated pulmonary metastases yields 5-year **post-relapse survival** rates of 30% to 40% in selected osteosarcoma patients. When all pulmonary nodules are anatomically resectable with adequate post-surgical respiratory reserve, repeated surgical thoracotomies or stereotactic ablative radiotherapy provide meaningful long-term disease-free intervals.

When all nodules are anatomically resectable, repeated resections provide meaningful long-term disease-free intervals.

left.title: Favourable Metastasectomy Candidates
points: Unilateral or limited bilateral discrete nodules
Prolonged disease-free interval (> 12 to 18 months)
Complete anatomical resectability confirmed on chest CT
Adequate baseline pulmonary spirometry reserve

right.title: Unfavourable Relapse Characteristics
points: Early relapse occurring during adjuvant MAP chemotherapy
Concomitant unresectable extrapulmonary or bone metastases
Extensive diffuse bilateral pleural or parenchymal seeding
Rapid tumour doubling kinetics indicating chemoresistance

steps.tx: Osteoclastic bone resorption driving osteolytic bone destruction is treatable with targeted monoclonal antibodies. **Giant cell tumour** of bone is characterized by neoplastic mononuclear stromal cells overexpressing **RANKL**, which recruits numerous reactive osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells causing extensive bone lysis. Targeted therapy with **denosumab**, a human monoclonal antibody against RANKL, halts osteoclastogenesis, promotes dense bone remineralisation, and reduces tumour volume.

rows: Improves event-free survival in localized disease
Disease stabilization in mutant central chondrosarcomas
